title: Ch 1–3 Unit Test
subtitle: Foundations of Gerontologic Nursing, Healthcare Policy & Assessment

groups.title: Chapter 2 · Healthcare Policy That Affects Older Adults
Chapter 3 · Assessment of the Older Adult

practiceExams.note: The study guides give no exam blueprint, question count, or time limit, so each unit test is 50 questions in 60 minutes, weighted by how much of Chapters 1-3 each section covers (Ch 1: 15, Ch 2: 17, Ch 3: 18) with 5 alternate-format items.

objectives.title: Chapter 1 · Overview of Gerontologic Nursing
items: Trace the historic development of gerontologic nursing as a specialty.
Identify the education, practice roles, and certification of the generalist, acute or primary care NP, and adult-gerontologic CNS.
Discuss the major U.S. demographic trends in the older adult population.
Describe how sex, marital status, race/ethnicity, living situation, education, economic status, and functional status affect health, well-being, and life expectancy.
Discuss how the aging of society will affect the future of healthcare delivery.
Explore ageism as it relates to the care of older adults in various settings.
Identify the issues influencing gerontologic nursing education.
Analyze the issues affecting gerontologic nursing research.

objectives.title: Chapter 2 · Healthcare Policy That Affects Older Adults
items: Discuss how the Standards of Practice for RNs guide their legal duties in caring for older adults.
State the sources and definitions of laws (statutes, regulations, case law) and the levels where they are made (federal, state, local).
Explore why older adults are a vulnerable population and the legal implications of that designation.
Discuss the reasons behind OBRA 1987 and its continuing effect on nursing facility residents and caregivers.
Identify OBRA's three major parts and the key areas in each.
State the rationale for the Affordable Care Act and who it was developed to benefit.
Discuss the legal history of autonomy and self-determination and the major laws involved.
Identify the three categories of elder abuse, define the seven types, and discuss the nurse's responsibility.
Name and state the purpose of advance directives and POLST.
Explain the purpose of the PSDA and the nurse's responsibility for advance directives.
Discuss ethical challenges in preparing patients for end-of-life decisions.

objectives.title: Chapter 3 · Assessment of the Older Adult
items: Explain how the physical and psychosocial aspects of aging interrelate in the assessment process.
Describe how the atypical presentation of illness affects assessment.
Compare the clinical presentation of delirium and dementia.
Describe the assessment modifications that may be necessary for older adults.
Describe strategies for collecting relevant, comprehensive health histories.
Identify the basic components of a health history for older adults.
List the principles for conducting physical examinations of older adults.
Explain the rationale for assessing functional status in older adults.
Describe the elements of a functional assessment.
Describe the basic components of cognitive assessment.
Explain the rationale for assessing social function.
Conduct a comprehensive health assessment on an older adult.
